zeta.enabled.description:
Enable or disable Zeta suggestions **for this window**.

**When to turn off:** temporarily disable suggestions (e.g. debugging the server) without uninstalling.
zeta.streamEnabled.description:
Stream completions over **SSE (Server-Sent Events)**. When enabled, tokens arrive incrementally but the ghost text is still rendered after the full response is received. Disable for cleaner log output with complete `prompt_eval`/`eval` statistics.

**When to enable:** network/remote server (faster first token) or debugging SSE. **When to keep off:** local server — complete `prompt_eval`/`eval` stats in logs are more useful.
zeta.temperature.description:
Sampling temperature for the model. Lower values (**0.0–0.2**) are more deterministic; higher values (**0.3–0.8**) increase creativity. Zeta edit-prediction models are typically used at **0.0–0.1** for stable, repetitive next-edit suggestions.

**Recommended ranges:** `0.0–0.2` stable/deterministic for everyday editing · `0.3–0.8` more creative · `0.0` strictly deterministic (best with `reuseIdenticalPromptResults`).
zeta.maxContextFiles.description:
**Maximum number** of related code excerpts to bundle into the prompt. For Zeta, LSP definitions/usages are preferred, then visible and recently-viewed files fill the remaining slots. Higher values give the model more cross-file context at the cost of a **longer prompt** and **slower first-token latency**.

**Recommended:** `3–8`. `0` disables cross-file context entirely. Higher values improve accuracy but add prompt length (slower first token).
zeta.outlineSymbols.description:
Optional number of nearby active-file LSP Document Symbols to include for **all model formats**. The compact `context/outline` section names the active class/function path (for example `CTextDraw::Draw`) and can include methods, fields, enum members, globals, and other useful symbols; this avoids sparse C/C++ outlines where the language server flattens methods. Symbols are ranked by distance from the cursor and restored to source order. Collection is fully asynchronous, never delays a completion, and refreshes for every resolved document version, including dirty buffers; an obsolete provider response is discarded. VS Code may still invoke the language server when its own Outline cache has no model for the current document version. This is a separate compact budget and does **not** consume `#zeta.maxContextFiles#`. Keep the default **`0`** to avoid Document Symbol provider work; set a positive value to opt in.

**Recommended:** `0` (off) for small files; `5–10` for large files; `10–20` for C/C++ (language servers flatten methods there). Costs a tiny async LSP call — no server-side cost.
zeta.maxEditHistory.description:
Total number of recent-edit diffs surfaced in the prompt. The budget is split: **~20%** reserved as a floor for the active file so its history survives long stints in other files, **~40%** spread across up to `#zeta.maxContextFiles#` other recent files, and the remainder fills from the active file's recent activity. Typing-burst edits on the same line within **60 s** are coalesced before counting against the budget.

**Recommended:** `10–20`. Larger budgets keep history for the active file at the cost of prompt size.
zeta.maxRecentChangesChars.description:
Maximum number of characters from formatted recent-edit history to include in the prompt. `#zeta.maxEditHistory#` limits the number of diff records, while this limits their rendered size so large paste/format/bulk edits cannot overflow small model contexts. **Set to `0`** to omit recent-edit history.

**Recommended:** `8000–16000`. `0` omits recent-edit history entirely.
zeta.maxClipboardLines.description:
Maximum lines of clipboard text to include as retrieval context. **Set to `0`** to disable clipboard context entirely. Clipboard content is emitted after code retrieval chunks.

**Recommended:** `10–40`. `0` disables clipboard context (privacy-friendly).
zeta.stableRetrievalOrdering.description:
Sort LSP/retrieval chunks **deterministically** by path and range. This can improve prefix-cache reuse when providers return equivalent results in a different order, at a possible cost to relevance ordering.

**When to enable:** your server has prompt caching (llama.cpp `-cpent`, vLLM/sglang) AND providers return chunks in varying order. **Keep off** when ordering changes are rare.
zeta.reuseIdenticalPromptResults.descrip:
Reuse a recent completion result when the complete prompt is byte-for-byte identical. Useful with deterministic temperature-0 models; **disabled by default**.

**When to enable:** temperature `0` with a prompt-cached server. **Keep off** otherwise — identical bytes are rare in editing.
zeta.identicalPromptCacheTtlMs.descripti:
**How long** an identical-prompt completion result may be reused when `zeta.reuseIdenticalPromptResults` is enabled.

**Recommended:** `3000–10000`. Shorter = fresher results, longer = more cache hits.
zeta.autocompleteExclusionPatterns.descr:
File globs / suffixes that Zeta should **never** request completions for. Defaults cover the common secret-bearing files (`.env`, `.pem`, `.key`, …) so request bodies don't leak credentials to the completion server. Add project-specific patterns to extend.

**Recommended:** keep the defaults (secret-bearing files). Add project-specific patterns such as `**/generated/**` to skip machine output.
zeta.autocompleteSnoozeUntil.description:
Pause completions until the given Unix timestamp (milliseconds). **`0` disables** the snooze. Set via the `Zeta: Snooze` command rather than editing this directly.

**How to use:** run the `Zeta: Snooze` command instead of editing this directly. `0` = not snoozed.
zeta.useCopilotStyleNextEditPresentation:
Use VS Code's proposed inline edit presentation for next-edit suggestions.

**⚠️ Warning:** this depends on VS Code proposed API. It **only works** in VS Code Insiders launched with `--enable-proposed-api=Yuuzuki.zeta-edit-prediction`; without that flag, VS Code may silently ignore the proposed inline completion fields.

**When to keep on:** you want the modern inline-edit overlay (green box + orange bar). **Turn off** to fall back to the legacy ghost-text/jump presentation; requires the proposed API flag either way (see README).
zeta.serverUrl.description:
Base URL of the OpenAI-compatible **`/v1/completions`** server serving the model — e.g. llama.cpp's `llama-server`, vLLM, sglang, Ollama with the OpenAI shim. The extension only POSTs to **`/v1/completions`**; nothing else on the server is touched.

**Recommended:** `http://localhost:8080` for a local llama.cpp/Ollama server; change the host/port to match your server (e.g. `http://10.126.126.1:8889` for a LAN GPU server).
zeta.modelName.description:
Model name sent in the request body's `model` field. The prompt format is auto-selected by substring match against this name:

- ****Zeta-2.1 (multi-region)**** — names containing `zeta-2.1`, `zeta2.1`, `zeta-2-1`, or `zeta_2_1`. Uses Zed V0318-style numbered boundaries such as `<|marker_1|>` / `<|marker_2|>` throughout one contiguous editable excerpt.
- ****Zeta-2 (single-region SeedCoder FIM)**** — names containing `zeta-2`, `zeta2`, or `seedcoder`. Uses the legacy git-conflict scaffold `<<<<<<< CURRENT` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> UPDATED`.
- **Zeta 2 (fallback)** — anything else. Uses the legacy format.

**Recommended:** the exact model name your server reports via `GET /v1/models`. The **Zeta-2.1** format (multi-region markers) is selected when the name contains `zeta-2.1` / `zeta2.1` — use it to get the best edit quality.
zeta.completionTimeoutMs.description:
Per-request timeout in milliseconds. Requests that exceed this are aborted and the suggestion is dropped. **Bump it up** for large prompts on slow hardware; **lower it** to fail fast on a misconfigured server.

**Recommended:** `8000–15000` for zeta-2.1 on desktop GPUs; `15000–30000` for CPU-only or far-away servers.
zeta.retriggerOnContextExit.description:
Request a fresh next-edit completion after the cursor moves **at least half** the height of the editable line window used by the last model request, even when the document text did not change. This keeps cursor navigation responsive for next-edit models without firing for small navigation steps. The request is debounced by `#zeta.contextExitRetriggerDebounceMs#`.

**When to enable:** you move the cursor a lot without typing (navigation-heavy editing). **Keep off** to save requests.
zeta.contextExitRetriggerDebounceMs.desc:
Delay in milliseconds before requesting a completion after the cursor has moved at least half the previous editable context window. Further cursor movement resets the timer; **`0`** requests on the next event-loop turn. Default `1500`, allowing normal editor navigation to settle before inference.

**Recommended:** `1000–2000`. `0` fires on the next event-loop turn (aggressive).
zeta.diagRadius.description:
Drop LSP diagnostics whose line is more than this many lines from the cursor before they reach the prompt.

- **`0`** disables the filter (every diagnostic on the file is kept, capped at 15 entries)
- Default **`12`** matches cursortab's behaviour and keeps the diagnostics block compact.

**Recommended:** `5–20`. `0` keeps every diagnostic on the file (capped at 15 entries).
zeta.rulesMaxChars.description:
Soft cap on the size of per-language instructions files (`.vscode/nes-<languageId>.md`).

Rules sit at the **front** of every completion prompt of every completion prompt — a prefix-cache-friendly slot, so a server with prompt caching (llama.cpp with `-cpent 256` to checkpoint every 256 tokens, vLLM/sglang prefix caching on by default) only re-evaluates the rules block on the first request or when the file changes. The cost of a fat rules file is therefore:

- **Context budget** consumed on every request, even when cached.
- **Prompt-eval latency spike** on first request and after every save.
- **No caching benefit at all** if your server has caching off or the threshold is set above the rules-block size.

Overflow surfaces as a Warning diagnostic + red background on the over-limit region in the editor; it does **not** truncate the file or block completions. **Set to `0`** to disable the warning.

Default `3000` ≈ ~1000 tokens on the Zeta tokenizer — a reasonable budget for session-stable guidance.

**Recommended:** `1500–5000`. `0` disables the size warning (rules still apply).
zeta.injectInlineDiagnostics.description:
****Mega-hack**: inline `// BUG:` comments next to every nearby diagnosed line in the prompt only.**

Appends `<commentPrefix> <marker> (code: <code>) - <message>` to each diagnosed line in the rendered prompt — inline placement next to the affected token gets the model to attend to LSP errors much more reliably than a sibling diagnostics section. The fake comments are stripped from the response before applying, anchored on the literal `<commentPrefix> <marker>` substring so the strip survives the model paraphrasing the rest of the message body.

**When to enable:**
- **✅** **0.5B / 1.5B ZetaAI checkpoints** — they routinely ignore the structured diagnostics section and need the inline nudge.
- **❌** **7B ZetaAI (default) and 8B Zeta-2 / Zeta-2.1 SeedCoder** — strong enough to pick up the structured block; the inline noise just bloats the prompt.

When on, the structured `context/diagnostics` section is suppressed so the same data isn't emitted twice.

**When to enable:** small checkpoints (0.5B/1.5B). **Keep off** for 7B+ models — the structured diagnostics section is enough.
zeta.inlineDiagnosticsMarker.description:
Marker phrase emitted between the language's comment prefix and the diagnostic body when `zeta.injectInlineDiagnostics` is on.

For C/C++ the default produces:
```
// BUG: LSP error here (code: undeclared_var_use_suggest) - use 'spdlog' instead (Use of undeclared identifier 'psdlog')
```

**Must be a phrase** a human would essentially never type a human would essentially never type — the response-side strip pinpoints our injections by matching the literal `<commentPrefix> <marker>` substring, so colliding with user-authored `TODO:` / `FIXME:` comments is undesirable. Different small models seem to attend to different phrasings; tune per model if the default doesn't get traction.

**Recommended:** keep the default `BUG: LSP error here`. Change only if your codebase already contains that literal phrase.
zeta.diagnosticsMessageTransforms.descri:
Additional regex transforms applied to every diagnostic message **after** the built-in normalisations.

Built-ins (**always active, can't be turned off**):
- Strip `(fix available)` / `(fixes available)` suffix
- Rewrite `did you mean 'X'?` → `use 'X' instead`
- Rewrite `consider using 'X'` → `use 'X' instead`
- Rewrite `replace with 'X'` → `use 'X' instead`

User entries:
- **Key** is a JavaScript regex source. Use `$1`, `$2`, … to reference capture groups in the replacement.
- **Value** is the replacement string.
- **Flags** are hardcoded to `i` (case-insensitive). For other flags, encode them in the pattern itself.
- Invalid regexes are silently skipped — a typo in one entry won't break the rest.

Applied uniformly to **both** the structured `context/diagnostics` section and the inline `// BUG:` injection. Defaults cover common clang / clang-tidy patterns; add entries for other linters as needed.

**Recommended:** keep the built-ins (always active). Add per-linter entries as needed; invalid regexes are silently skipped.
zeta.editableTokens.description:
Approximate total token budget for the active current-file context. Zeta estimates **1 token per **3 UTF-8 bytes**** and keeps complete lines. For Zeta, this controls the leading broad-context section with a **2/3 before cursor / 1/3 after cursor** target; unused budget is used on the available side at a file boundary. For Zeta-2 / Zeta-2.1, it controls the line-aligned editable excerpt. Default `**2500**` — keep it well below half the server's context window (`/v1/models` reports `n_ctx`).

**Ranges:** `1000–1500` small/quick prompts · `2000–3000` balanced (default `2500`) · `4000–5000` maximum — keep **below half the server `n_ctx`** or requests will fail.
zeta.zetaContextTokens.description:
Approximate total token budget for additional non-editable current-file context around the Zeta-2.1 editable excerpt. It uses the same cheap ****UTF-8 bytes / 3**** estimate and whole-line boundaries. Context before the edit is placed in the FIM prefix; context after it is placed in the FIM suffix. **Set to `0`** to disable this surrounding context. Default `150` follows the Zeta V0318 provider profile.

**Recommended:** `100–300`. `0` disables the surrounding context (aggressive prompt shrinking).
zeta.maxTokens.description:
Maximum number of tokens the model is allowed to generate per request (`max_tokens` / `n_predict`). The model rewrites the entire editable window even on a single-line change, so a low value truncates the response mid-window and the extension **discards** truncated responses truncated responses (finishReason=length). Default `2048` is generous enough that healthy responses never hit this cap. Reduce carefully if you observe the model generating excessively long completions.

**Recommended:** keep `2048`. Lower to `1024` only if you often see timeouts from very long completions — but a truncated response (finishReason=length) is **discarded**, so too-low values break large edits.
zeta.syntaxAwareExpansion.description:
Enables syntax-aware editable-window expansion. Uses bracket-depth heuristics to enclose the cursor's function/block/class boundary instead of plain line-by-line expansion. Requires **no language server** required. The quality improvement is most noticeable for code inside well-bracketed blocks.

**When to keep on:** you work in well-bracketed languages (TS/JS/Rust/C/Go). **Keep off** if you notice odd window boundaries in unusual formats.
zeta.suggestionCacheThreshold.descriptio:
Fixed-line threshold for cursor-move-back re-show. When the cursor returns within this many lines of the original request position, the cached suggestion is re-shown **instantly** without a new request. Only used when `useEditRangeForCache` is disabled.

**Recommended:** `3–5`. Larger = more forgiving cursor moves re-show the suggestion; too large can show stale suggestions.
zeta.useEditRangeForCache.description:
Use the edit's actual line range (plus `editRangeMargin`) to decide cursor-move-back re-show eligibility, instead of a fixed offset from the request line. Large edits are **more forgiving** — the cursor can be far from the request line and still trigger a re-show if it stays inside the edit body.

**Recommended:** leave **on** — edit-range matching is smarter than a fixed offset (big edits are more forgiving).
zeta.editRangeMargin.description:
Extra lines added around the edit range when `useEditRangeForCache` is enabled. A margin of `3` means the cursor can be **up to 3 lines** before the edit start or after the edit end and still re-show the cached suggestion.

**Recommended:** `3–5`. `0` restricts re-show to strictly inside the edit range.
zeta.skipDebounceOnAccept.description:
Skip the input debounce right after a suggestion is accepted, so the follow-up prediction request fires **immediately** without waiting for the debounce timeout. Makes consecutive accept → predict cycles feel snappier.

**When to keep on:** you accept suggestions frequently and want the next prediction ASAP. Tiny extra load per accept.
